tested: the two laws: Chile's Decree 521 of 1999 (minimum strengths of 30, 35, 40 and 43 per cent for Corriente, Especial, Reservado and Gran Pisco, a rest of 60 days, discontinuous alembics, guarda for 180 days in wood) and Peru's denomination of 1990 (Resolución Directoral 072087 of 12 December 1990) with PromPerú's rest of at least three months. 4 searches.

pisco-porton: the rename to Caravedo, the TTAB cancellation of 2017, the distillery's range and acholado sheet (Quebranta, Torontel, Albilla, 43 per cent, three years on one vintage's sheet), the house's and tasters' notes. 4 searches.

barsol: the buyers and year of 2002, the closure of 1968 and the 34 idle years, the copper pot stills, 41.3 per cent, the name BarSol, exports by 2005, the Puro Quebranta name on the importer's pages and its 2l release of July 2026, the importer's tasting note against Difford's. 4 searches.

macchu-pisco: 2006 and the two sisters, Quebranta alone, copper pot stills, the year's rest and bottling at the estate on the house's own pages, the strength (40, 42 or 44 by source), the house's note, La Diablada and Ñusta. 3 searches.

capel: the founding at Paihuano in February 1938 by 25 growers, the legal standing of 1939, the 1964 name (not found), the Vicuña plant, the Transparente's Pedro Jiménez, double distillation and year in steel, the Reservado de Guarda's six to eight months in American oak, the taste. 5 searches.

el-gobernador: the launch of 2012 against Torres's 1928, Moscatel of Alexandria and pink Moscatel, a single discontinuous distillation in copper, 40 per cent, the governor Felipe Margutt Donaire and his dates (not found), Torres 10's solera and American oak. 3 searches.
22 of the 28 searches spent; 6 left unused.

Cards and questions of all five: one right answer each, wrong options of one kind, keys at positions 2, 0, 0, 3, 3, 1, 0, 2, 2, 1 (no position more than three times), each explain naming the nearest wrong option. Macchu Pisco's founding card no longer asks two things at once; BarSol's revival card and stem no longer name the buyers. No card id changed.

changed.was: The distillery's page gives three years of rest before bottling; no age statement.
changed.now: it rests in vessels that give it no flavour before it is bottled. No age statement.
changed.why: the three years sit on the distillery's sheet for one vintage (2020), not as a rule of the bottling

changed.was: a floral nose of roses and herbs over ripe mandarin, lime and raisin; then a sweet, dense palate and a finish of flowers and lemon verbena
changed.now: a floral nose over sweet ripe fruit, a sweet and dense palate, and a floral, herbal finish; tasters often add orange blossom, citrus, cinnamon and a little white pepper
changed.why: roses, mandarin, lime and raisin were found in no source; the house's sheet gives the floral nose, ripe fruit, dense palate and herbal finish, and the other notes come from trade and tasters' notes

changed.was: reached American shelves as Caravedo, while in Peru the bottle kept the Portón name
changed.now: came to American shelves as Caravedo, the distillery's own name
changed.why: a present state that will not hold: Spirits Hunters reports the rename announced for every market

changed.was: comes in seven single grapes ... aromatic grapes, one pass through the still
changed.now: was made in seven single grapes ... a blend of grapes, one pass through the still
changed.why: a present range is a fact that ages, and the acholado holds Quebranta, a non aromatic grape

changed.was: two Peruvian partners bought it in 2002
changed.now: a group of investors based in the United States bought it in 2002 (the card and stem: taken on by new investors)

changed.was: It had lain idle for decades
changed.why: the importer dates the closure to 1968 and Distiller counts 34 idle years before 2002

changed.was: They called the pisco BarSol, and by 2005
changed.now: They called the pisco BarSol, for the sun of Ica and the bars of the world, as the house tells it, and by 2005
changed.why: the name's meaning is the house's own account, repeated by Difford's Guide

changed.was: then cream and cocoa on the palate, and a round, long finish

41.8 per cent was found in no source read

changed.now: Peru had made pisco its denomination of origin in 1990, binding it to the grapes, the single distillation and the rest without wood.
changed.why: a filing teaches nothing behind a bar; the denomination of 1990 keeps two years in the story and stands in IPONZ's register and El Peruano

changed.was: rested a year in vessels that give it nothing, as Peru's rules require ... Two siblings followed the plain bottling
changed.now: rested a year, by the house's account, in vessels that give it nothing ... Two other bottlings show
changed.why: Peru requires a rest, not a year; the year is the house's; the order of release was not confirmed

changed.now: In which year was Macchu Pisco founded?

tension: plan.json, capel why: says the cooperative was formed at Vicuña and that its pisco is made from muscat grapes, and counts its members as now over a thousand; it was formed at Paihuano, the Transparente is Pedro Jiménez, and a count of members ages. Reported, not edited.

plan.json, pisco-porton why: says the Mosto Verde is an acholado; the house makes seven single grape mosto verdes beside the acholado, which is why the record names the Acholado. Reported, not edited.

The Library (Caravedo / Pisco Porton): calls Peru's pisco rules the strictest anywhere, a judgement; says the old stone fermentation vats remain in use, found in no source; and spells flavor in the American way. Reported, not edited.

The liquor shelf, El Gobernador: names Felipe Margutt Donaire with no dates, which the brief's rule for the dead does not allow, and says Reservado means 40% ABV where the decree makes 40 the minimum, below Gran Pisco at 43. Reported, not edited.
